extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering dataset consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. Annotators are presented with a question and a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotate a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or mark null if no long/short answer is present.
extraction.creator: Google Research
extraction.citeAs: Kwiatkowski, T., Palomaki, J., Redfield, O., Collins, M., Parikh, A., Alberti, C., Epstein, D., Polosukhin, I., Devlin, J., Lee, K., Toutanova, K., Jones, L., Kelcey, M., Chang, M.-W., Dai, A. M., Uszkoreit, J., & Le, Q. (2019). Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 7, 453–466.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream. Annotators are presented with a (question, Wikipedia page) pair and annotate a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or mark null if no long/short answer is present.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: 51% of examples have no long answer labeled, and 64% have no short answer labeled.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, paired with Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream. Questions are paired with Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results. Annotators follow comprehensive guidelines to identify long and short answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators are presented with a (question, Wikipedia page) pair and annotate a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or mark null if no long/short answer is present. Annotators follow a decision flow with three stages: Question Identification, Long Answer Identification, and Short Answer Identification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 25-way annotations on 302 examples were used to study variability in annotations. For long answers, the most popular long answer accounts for 83% of annotations, and the two most popular account for 96%. For short answers, the most popular accounts for 64%, and the three most popular account for 90%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and 7,842 examples with 5-way annotations sequestered as test data.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators are a pool of around 50 annotators with an average annotation time of 80 seconds. Specific demographics are not provided in the paper.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available and maintained by Google Research. Versioning information, updating timeframe, maintainers, and deprecation policies are not explicitly discussed.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, but no explicit mention of sensitive human attributes collected.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to drive research in natural language understanding and question answering systems, which can have significant utility to users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on Wikipedia as a source of factual information, which may introduce biases. The paper acknowledges that there may be biases in this choice and suggests future data collection efforts may introduce shorter queries or domains other than Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may have biases due to the focus on Wikipedia. The task is designed to be close to an end-to-end question answering application, but systems still have a large gap to close compared to human upper bounds.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Benchmarking for question answering systems. The dataset is designed to provide large-scale end-to-end training data for the QA problem and drive research in natural language understanding.
